definitions.explanation: Something that is kept hidden from others.

examples.japanese: これは{秘密|ひみつ}だよ。
{友達|ともだち}に{秘密|ひみつ}を{打|う}ち{明|あ}けた。
examples.english: I confided a secret to my friend.

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}だけの{秘密|ひみつ}にしようと{約束|やくそく}したのに、みんなに{知|し}られてしまった。
examples.english: We promised to keep it a secret between just the two of us, but everyone found out.

notes:
{秘密|ひみつ} means a secret or confidential matter. It functions as a noun and can modify other nouns with の ({秘密|ひみつ}の{場所|ばしょ}, a secret place).

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {秘密|ひみつ}を{守|まも}る: to keep a secret
- {秘密|ひみつ}にする: to keep something secret
- {秘密|ひみつ}を{明|あ}かす: to reveal a secret
- {秘密|ひみつ}を{打|う}ち{明|あ}ける: to confide a secret
- {秘密|ひみつ}を{漏|も}らす: to leak a secret

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ないしょ ({内緒|ないしょ}): casual word for secret, often used among friends and family
- {極秘|ごくひ}: top secret, strictly confidential (formal/official)

NOTE:
{秘密|ひみつ} is neutral in register and works in both casual and formal contexts. ないしょ is softer and more colloquial — ないしょにしてね is the casual equivalent of {秘密|ひみつ}にしておいて.
